key_insight: NemotronLabs VoiceChat is an open, full-duplex speech-to-speech model that can talk and listen at the same time while also calling tools natively. It unifies transcription, reasoning, function calling, and speech synthesis in one streaming system.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of building voice assistants that are not only real-time and conversational, but also capable of structured tool use without breaking the flow of speech.
method: Uses a streaming speech encoder paired with a decoder-only language model for continuous understanding and generation.
Produces parallel output streams for agent text and structured function calls to support tool invocation during conversation.
Adds an auxiliary RNN-T branch for incremental user transcription and a streaming TTS decoder for low-latency spoken responses.
impact: This matters because it brings voice agents closer to natural human conversation while enabling actionable tool use in a single pipeline. For practitioners, it points to a practical architecture for building responsive, multimodal, tool-using assistants.

paper_title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities
paper_authors: Jagadeesh Balam, Travis Bartley, Edresson Casanova, Sanjay Chauhan, Chen Chen
